newsitem.title: USA: US offers $2 mln reward in al-Hayat bomb case.
newsitem.headline: US offers $2 mln reward in al-Hayat bomb case.

text.p: The United States on Thursday offered a $2 million reward for information leading to those responsible for four letter bombs sent to the Washington offices of the al-Hayat newspaper last January.

"It's clear to us that the people who were responsible for this letter bomb campaign intended to conduct a terrorism campaign in the United States and this is one of those important steps that we can in fact take to find the perpetrators," Greg Bujac, director of diplomatic security at the State Department, said at a briefing.
The reward will be publicized with posters and matchbooks, Bujac said.

Four letter bombs, disguised inside musical Christmas cards and bearing improvised explosive devices, were all sent to offices of al-Hayat at the National Press Club, U.S. officials said. All were postmarked Alexandria, Egypt and dated Dec. 21.
Similar bombs were sent to the newspaper's offices at the United Nations in New York City and in London.
The London-based newspaper, owned by a member of the Saudi royal family, has a reputation as one of the most objective newspapers in the Arab world.
